brief:
Britain announced new sanctions targeting Israeli settlements, but the measures include significant carve-outs that limit their practical impact, according to Mondoweiss. Components for F-35 fighter jets remain exempt from the restrictions, and the sanctions do not target Israel's state apparatus. Enforcement will not begin for months, further delaying any concrete consequences.

The sanctions mark a shift in British policy toward Israeli settlements but fall short of comprehensive action against settlement expansion. Critics note the exemptions undercut the measures' deterrent effect, leaving core elements of Israel's military and state operations untouched.
dek: The UK's new sanctions on Israeli settlements may be groundbreaking, but they're also full of loopholes. F-35 parts are exempt, the state itself is untouched, and enforcement won't start for months. Real progress, but far from enough.
title: UK settlement sanctions contain major exemptions, enforcement delayed
